## What this document does

The sample size was based on a simulation-based power analysis for the specific benefit of
prequestions on the final test, using the `mixedpower` package [@kumle2021] with pilot data
collected in the lab. A recent meta-analysis reported a medium-sized specific benefit
(*g* = 0.54; @sthilaire2023), which corresponds to an odds ratio of 2.66 and a log odds of
0.98. This was used as the smallest effect size of interest (SESOI) for the effect of
Condition (prequestioned vs. non-prequestioned topic) in binomial mixed models of the points
earned on each topic, fitted separately to the pilot participants given Polio and TB
prequestions.

The simulations indicated that 45 participants per group give 90% power to detect an effect
of this size. Because the study has three groups rather than two and also analyses eye
movements, we planned to test 135 participants (45 per group).

This document is not part of the analysis pipeline (`_targets.R`): it reproduces the
sample-size planning that preceded data collection. It is rendered on its own, from the
project root: `quarto render power/power_analysis.qmd`.

**Packages.** `mixedpower` is installed from GitHub, not CRAN, and `hypr` [@rabe2020] (for the
contrast coding) from CRAN; install them once before rendering:

```r
install.packages(c("remotes", "hypr"))
remotes::install_github("DejanDraschkow/mixedpower")
```

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(hypr)         # contrast coding
library(mixedpower)   # simulation-based power for (G)LMMs (Kumle et al., 2021)
```

## Pilot data

Each pilot participant answered the ten final-test questions, five per topic; each topic was
worth 12 points.

```{r}
#| label: data
scored <- read_csv(here("power", "pilot_reading1.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  select(Participant, Group, Condition, poin, Text, Acc)

# Participants given prequestions (Polio or TB group)
scored_pbtb <- scored |>
  filter(Group %in% c("TB", "Polio")) |>
  mutate(Condition = factor(Condition), Group = factor(Group))

# Condition (question topic): TB vs. Polio; Group: Polio vs. TB
contrasts(scored_pbtb$Condition) <- contr.hypothesis(hypr(TB ~ Polio, levels = c("Polio", "TB")))
contrasts(scored_pbtb$Group) <- contr.hypothesis(hypr(Polio ~ TB, levels = c("Polio", "TB")))

# Points earned per participant and topic (out of 12), separately for each group
by_topic <- \(grp) scored_pbtb |>
  filter(Group == grp) |>
  group_by(Group, Participant, Condition) |>
  summarise(score_count = sum(Acc), total = 12, .groups = "drop")
s <- by_topic("TB")
d <- by_topic("Polio")

count(scored_pbtb, Group) |> mutate(participants = n / 10)
```

## Models

Binomial mixed models of the points earned on each topic, with random intercepts for
participants, fitted separately to the TB and Polio groups.

```{r}
#| label: models
model_tb <- glmer(cbind(score_count, total - score_count) ~ Condition + (1 | Participant),
                  family = binomial, data = s)
model_po <- glmer(cbind(score_count, total - score_count) ~ Condition + (1 | Participant),
                  family = binomial, data = d)
summary(model_po)$coefficients
summary(model_tb)$coefficients
```

## Simulation

The SESOI replaces the model's estimates: −0.25 for the intercept and 0.98 (log odds; the
meta-analytic *g* = 0.54) for the Condition effect. Power is estimated for 30, 40, and 50
participants, with a critical value of |*z*| = 1.96.

```{r}
#| label: simulation
SESOI <- c(-0.25, 0.98)   # intercept, Condition (log odds)

power_po <- mixedpower(model = model_po, data = d, fixed_effects = c("Condition"),
                       simvar = "Participant", steps = c(30, 40, 50), critical_value = 1.96,
                       SESOI = SESOI, n_sim = params$n_sim, databased = FALSE)
power_tb <- mixedpower(model = model_tb, data = s, fixed_effects = c("Condition"),
                       simvar = "Participant", steps = c(30, 40, 50), critical_value = 1.96,
                       SESOI = SESOI, n_sim = params$n_sim, databased = FALSE)
power_po
power_tb
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-power
#| fig-cap: "Estimated power by number of participants, Polio and TB groups"
multiplotPower(power_po)
multiplotPower(power_tb)
```
